subjects.name: Policing in the northern United States

summary: How police in the northern United States grew from for-profit constables and corrupt ward-boss enforcers in the 1800s into forces that protected the wealthy and broke strikes, alongside the Pinkertons and the Pennsylvania State Police.

evidence.note: 1837 Broad Street Riot in Boston used to justify the first formal police department in 1838
for-profit, contingency-fee constables in New York and Boston in the early 1800s
ward leaders running vice rackets, gangs and police; systematic bribery and vote rigging
anti-Irish bigotry, first Irish officer and the Know Nothing takeover in Massachusetts
unions and strikes of the late 1800s recast as riots; public order arrests and tramp acts
Pennsylvania State Police founded after the anthracite strike, modelled on the Philippine Constabulary
1906 Windber strike: state police kill miners and a boy; latest period told at length
Allan Pinkerton's life and the founding and strikebreaking of his agency
long account of the 1892 Homestead Strike and the battle with the Pinkerton barges
Pinkerton under Securitas spying on workers today; with state police search data, sets reaches_present

notes: Part two of the Behind the Police mini-series. The host dates the Pennsylvania State Police to 1903; it was created in 1905. Modern material (2002-2020 state police search data, Pinkerton's current labor surveillance) is short, so it sets reaches_present rather than extending covered_span. Covered start 1800 approximates the early-1800s constable system.
